- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model often fails to revert to 30-day moving average; align forecast to 14-day MA if sentiment <0.5.
- When official events are frequent (≥20 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to underestimate price volatility; increase forecast standard deviation by 10–20% for risk-adjusted output.
